See below. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # The [[beginning]] of an activity. #: {{ux|en|The movie was entertaining from '''start''' to finish.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|act=3|scene=i|passage=I see you stand like greyhounds in the slips, / Straining upon the '''start'''.}} # A sudden involuntary [[movement]]. #: {{ux|en|He woke with a '''start'''.}} #* {{RQ:L'Estrange Fables of Aesop|passage=Nature does nothing by '''starts''' and leaps, or in a hurry.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1885|author=w:Robert Louis Stevenson|title={{w|Olalla (short story)|Olalla}} |passage=The sight of his scared face, his '''starts''' and pallors and sudden harkenings, unstrung me {{...}}}} # The beginning [[point]] of a [[race]], a [[board game]], etc. #: {{ux|en|Captured pieces are returned to the '''start''' of the board.}} # An [[appearance]] in a sports game, horserace, etc., from the beginning of the event. #: {{ux|en|Jones has been a substitute before, but made his first '''start''' for the team last Sunday.}} # {{lb|en|horticulture}} A young [[plant]] [[germinate]]d in a pot to be [[transplant]]ed later. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Liz Primeau; Steven A. Frowine|title=Gardening Basics For Canadians For Dummies |passage=You generally see nursery '''starts''' at garden centres in mid to late spring. Small annual plants are generally sold in four-packs or larger packs, with each cell holding a single young plant.}} # An initial advantage over somebody else; a [[head start]]. #: {{ux|en|to get, or have, the '''start'''}} #* {{RQ:Bramah Max Carrados|passage=The man has got two clear days' '''start''' and the chances are nine to one against catching him.}} # {{lb|en|UK|slang|archaic}} A {{inh|en|enm|sterten|t=to leap up suddenly, rush out}}, from {{inh|en|ang|styrtan|t=to leap up, start}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sturtijan|t=to startle, move, set in motion}}, from Cognate with {{cog|ofs|stirta|t=to fall down, tumble}}, {{cog|dum|sterten|t=to rush, fall, collapse}} ({{cog|nl|storten}}), {{cog|goh|sturzen|t=to hurl, plunge, turn upside down}} ({{cog|de|stürzen}}), {{cog|goh|sterzan|t=to be stiff, protrude}}. More at {{l|en|stare}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|ergative}} To [[begin]], [[commence]], [[initiate]]. ## To set in [[motion]]. ##: {{ux|en|to '''start''' a stream of water;   to '''start''' a rumour;   to '''start''' a business}} ##* '''April 2, 1716''', {{w|Joseph Addison}}, ''Freeholder'' No. 30 ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=22|passage=In the autumn there was a row at some cement works about the unskilled labour men. A union had just been '''started''' for them and all but a few joined. One of these blacklegs was laid for by a picket and knocked out of time.}} ## To [[begin]]. ##: {{ux|en|The President fired the gun to '''start''' the footrace.}} ##: {{ux|en|The rain '''started''' at 9:00.}} ##* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage=Thinks I to myself, “Sol, you're run off your course again. This is a rich man's summer ‘cottage’ {{...}}.” So I '''started''' to back away again into the bushes. But I hadn't backed more'n a couple of yards when I see something so amazing that I couldn't help scooching down behind the bayberries and looking at it.}} ## {{senseid|en|to initiate operation of a vehicle or machine}}To [[ready]] the operation of a vehicle or machine. ##: {{ux|en|to '''start''' the engine}} ## To put or raise (a question, an objection); to put forward (a subject for discussion). ## To bring onto being or into view; to originate; to invent. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1674|author={{w|Sir William Temple, 1st Baronet|William Temple}}|title=letter to The Countess of Essex |passage=Sensual men agree in the pursuit of every pleasure they can '''start'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[have]] its [[origin]] (at), [[begin]]. #: {{ux|en|The speed limit is 50 km/h, '''starting''' at the edge of town.}} #: {{ux|en|The blue line '''starts''' one foot away from the wall.}} # To move suddenly, from a previous state of rest; to [[startle]]. ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[jerk]], [[jump]] up, [[flinch]], or draw back in [[surprise]]. ##: {{syn|en|jump}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|act=V|scene=v|passage=But if he '''start''',
It is the flesh of a corrupted heart.}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|act=I|scene=v|page=257|column=2|passage=I could a Tale vnfold, vvhoſe lighteſt vvord
VVould harrovv vp thy ſoule, freeze thy young blood,
Make thy tvvo eyes like Starres, '''ſtart''' from their Spheres,
Thy knotty and combined locks to part,
And each particular haire to ſtand an end,
Like Quilles vpon the fretfull Porpentine: {{...}}}} ##* {{RQ:Dryden Spanish Fryar|passage=I '''start''' as from some dreadful dream.}} ##* {{RQ:Watts Logick|text=Keep your soul to the work when it is ready to '''start''' aside.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1855|author=w:Robert Browning|title=s:Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came|section=XXXI |passage=[...] The tempest's mocking elf
Points to the shipman thus the unseen shelf
He strikes on, only when the timbers '''start'''.}} ##* {{RQ:Wilde Dorian Gray|chapter=VIII|page=139|passage=Suddenly his eye fell on the screen that he had placed in front of the portrait, and he '''started'''.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1836|author=Elizur Wright|magazine=Quarterly Anti-slavery Magazine|volume=2|page=162 |passage=Physical poison would make them '''start''' from arsenicked bread; shall not the moral poison which is in it, make them '''start''' more promptly still from slave produce?}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[awaken]] suddenly. ##* {{RQ:Mary Shelley Frankenstein|volume=I|chapter=IV|page=100|passage=I '''started''' from my sleep with horror; a cold dew covered my forehead, my teeth chattered, and every limb became convulsed; [...]}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[disturb]] and set in motion; to [[alarm]]; to [[rouse]]; to cause to flee. ##: {{ux|en|The hounds '''started''' a fox.}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|I|i|text=Upon malicious bravery dost thou come
To '''start''' my quiet?}} ## {{lb|en|ergative|of an object}} To come loose, to break free of a firmly set position; to [[displace]] or [[loosen]]; to [[dislocate]]. ##: {{ux|en|the storm '''started''' the bolts in the vessel}} ##* {{RQ:Wiseman Chirurgicall Treatises|passage=One, by a fall in wrestling, '''started''' the end of the clavicle from the sternon.}} ##* {{RQ:Cleland Fanny Hill|1|76|[...] we could, with the greateſt eaſe, as well as clearneſs, ſee all objects, (ourſelves unſeen) only by applying our eyes cloſe to the crevice, where the moulding of a pannel had warp'd, or '''ſtarted''' a little on the other ſide.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|sports}} To put into play. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Brian Glanville|title=The Story of the World Cup: The Essential Companion to South Africa 2010|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=gdhvSSP-2kAC&pg=PA361|page=361|publisher=Faber and Faber|location=London|isbn=9780571236053 |passage=The charge against Zagallo then is not so much that he '''started''' Ronaldo, but that when it should surely have been clear that the player was in no fit state to take part he kept him on.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Sid Lowe|title=Portu’s brilliant burst seals Girona’s top-four fairytale in the perfect way|date=2024-05-06|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/06/girona-barcelona-champions-league-la-liga-portu-michel|passage= “Look at Portu,” Michel insisted, “he scores goals and I never '''start''' him. He says: ‘You’re sinking me, but OK, I’ll just go out and score again.’”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013071057/https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/06/girona-barcelona-champions-league-la-liga-portu-michel|archivedate=13 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|transitive|nautical}} To pour out; to empty; to tap and begin drawing from. #: {{ux|en|to '''start''' a water cask}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|euphemistic}} To begin one's [[menstruation|menstrual cycle]]. #: {{ux|en|Have you '''started''' yet?}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|possibly|_|obsolete}} To [[begin]] a [[journey]]; to [[set forth]]. #* {{RQ:en:CSL|volume=1|page=5|text=I GET letters from you far too seldom considering that you can much more easily find people '''starting''' for Rome than I to Athens: considering, too, that you are more certain of my being at Rome than I of your being at Athens.}} =====Usage notes===== * In uses 1.1 and 1.2 this is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the infinitive {{qualifier|to}} or the gerund {{qualifier|-ing}} form.
